Script-visible WebGPU error scopes for the scripted binding: native device work runs in validation, out-of-memory and internal device scopes and routes what they catch to the script's own scope, so script sees its errors and the uncaptured-error callback stays quiet. Vellum wrote this; Pulp's binding runs no error scopes.

The sealed V8 provider's consumer_defines, applied to the imported target so every translation unit that includes V8 headers compiles with the library's ABI. Pulp's tools/cmake/PulpV8ConsumerDefines.cmake respelled under Vellum names; the Pulp spelling would raise the framework name debt.

Resolves the sealed V8 provider for VELLUM_ENABLE_V8 from Vellum's dependency lock: the digest-checked v8-builder archive, its manifest paired with the renderer lock's Skia and Dawn, and a per-file receipt. Vellum's counterpart to Pulp's tools/cmake/FindV8.cmake for its one platform.

Frame-level render pass manager: ordered background, content, effects, overlay and post-effect passes with a per-frame time budget and the whole-recording GPU render time, read by the inspector, the motion cost view and the UI preview. Distinct from the custom GPU pass API of Generous-Corp/vellum#432.
Pulp's AT-SPI provider with character-based text offsets, Component calls that honor the requested coordinate space, and a GetAll that returns every property Get serves.
Pulp's Linux text accessibility backend with the test-hook symbol respelled vellum_text_accessibility_role_linux (and its parameter role_value), which carries no Pulp spelling here.
Pulp's outbound file drag backend, running the XDND handshake on the connection it opens, with a protocol source window created there.
Pulp's XDND parsing helpers plus the pure reply validation and version negotiation the drag source uses.
Pulp's XDND drag-source handshake with a protocol source window on the pumped connection, replies checked against the current target, and version-specific completion.
AT-SPI2 role, state and interface constants the Linux accessibility provider maps onto.
Pulp's Linux clipboard backend that blocks SIGPIPE on the writing thread and consumes the signal it caused, so it never changes the process-wide disposition.
Pulp's Linux environment adapter that classifies memory pressure through a helper which treats a parsed MemAvailable of zero as critical and a missing field as no reading.
File dialogs through the desktop portal over D-Bus on Linux.
Pulp's Avahi backend with one lock order between browse and the Avahi callbacks, and resolvers tracked per browse so a stop or destruction frees them and a result from an earlier browse is dropped.
Pulp's libnotify backend that installs only when notify_init succeeds, reports availability from that result, and replaces a notification posted again under the same id instead of orphaning it.
Pure /proc/meminfo parsing and memory-pressure classification for the Linux environment adapter.
Pure UTF-8 offset arithmetic between the byte text of a View and the character offsets AT-SPI uses.
